locations.name: Frozen Tundra
locations.brief: A harsh, frozen tundra where the story opens.
locations.description: A snow-covered, windswept tundra under a flat, colorless sky; the wind carries stinging grains of ice.
locations.current_state: Cold and windswept; snow is settling into exposed clothing.

locations.name: Dark Rock Rise
locations.brief: A low, broken rise of dark rock to the west on the frozen tundra.
locations.description: A low, broken rise of dark rock to the west of the Time Traveler's position; he crossed it at a stumble and from its crest saw the mammoth carcass lying in the white beyond.
locations.current_state: Crossed by the Time Traveler; on its far side lie the dead mammoth and the ravine.

locations.name: The Ravine
locations.brief: A ravine beyond the rise, followed down by the Time Traveler to a narrow seam of shadow.
locations.description: A ravine beyond the rise of dark rock; from the tundra it appeared only as a shadow. Followed down, it narrows and its walls rise until they pinch to a seam of shadow where split stone leans together.
locations.current_state: Followed down by the Time Traveler; its walls narrow and rise to a seam of shadow where the shallow overhang lies.

locations.name: The Shallow Overhang
locations.brief: A shallow shelf of rock in a seam of the ravine where split stone breaks the wind.
locations.description: A shallow overhang where the ravine's stone has split and one slab leans against another; no more than a shelf of rock, but it breaks the wind. Its mouth has been sealed with a low wall of packed snow with the rib shard wedged upright at its base.
locations.current_state: Night; the Time Traveler is inside behind the low snow wall, and an unseen animal is circling and sniffing outside.

entities.name: The Jump
entities.brief: The time jump whose afterimage and nausea the Time Traveler experienced on waking.
entities.description: The time-travel jump that left an afterimage behind the Time Traveler's eyes and nausea rolling through him in thin waves.

entities.name: The Time Traveler's Coat
entities.brief: A coat worn by the Time Traveler, now bearing the smell of mammoth fat.
entities.description: The Time Traveler's coat; snow had settled into its folds and seams on the tundra, and mammoth fat from the carcass is now on it.
entities.current_state: Mammoth fat from the carcass is on it; the thing outside can smell it.

entities.name: The Woolly Mammoth Carcass
entities.brief: A whole, unmarked woolly mammoth lying dead in the snow beyond the rise.
entities.description: A dark mound in the white, too regular to be rock; snow had drifted against one flank and the matted coat held the animal's shape like a cast. Its trunk lay curled against the snow and one tusk was sheared near the root. The body was whole, with no cuts, no spear marks and no trampled ring where hunters had stood; nothing had fed on it. It had lain down, or been caught, and the cold had kept it.
entities.current_state: Dead and preserved by the cold; a rib shard and a strip of hide have been taken from it.

entities.name: Rib Shard and Hide Strip
entities.brief: A mammoth rib shard wedged at the overhang mouth, and a hide strip wrapped around the Time Traveler's wrist.
entities.description: A shard of rib worked free from the mammoth carcass, now wedged upright at the mouth of the overhang with snow packed against its base; a strip of hide torn from the flank, stiff as board, wrapped around the Time Traveler's wrist.
entities.current_state: Rib shard wedged upright at the overhang mouth with snow packed at its base; hide strip still wrapped around the Time Traveler's wrist.

entities.name: The Device
entities.brief: A small device, like a river stone, that gave no response when the Time Traveler pressed its charger.
entities.description: A small device that lay in the Time Traveler's palm like a river stone, small and certain. It has a charger; when pressed, its cold glass gave no glow, no hum, and no answer, even after a third attempt.
entities.current_state: Unresponsive after three attempts; put away by the Time Traveler.

entities.name: The Thing Outside
entities.brief: An unseen heavy animal circling the overhang at night, drawn by the smell of mammoth fat.
entities.description: A weight moving over snow outside the overhang, deliberate and circling. It stopped and sniffed; the mammoth's fat on the Time Traveler's coat drew it, and it did not leave. Its kind is not seen or identified.
entities.current_state: Circling and sniffing outside the snow wall; has not left.

chapters.text:
Cold woke him first, before memory did — a cold so total it seemed less a temperature than a subtraction, as though something essential had been drawn out of him and replaced with glass. He lay on his back in the white, and the sky above was a flat, colorless lid. His teeth ached. Behind his eyes a slow pulse beat, the afterimage of the jump, nausea rolling through him in thin waves.

He pushed himself up on one elbow. The snow had begun to settle into the folds of his coat, into the seams, patient as a thief. He knew the arithmetic of this: skin to shivering, shivering to numbness, numbness to a sleep that did not end. Hours. Perhaps fewer.

He got his knees under him. The wind came across the tundra without hurry, carrying grains of ice that stung his cheek, and he turned from it, scanning. A rise of dark rock to the west, low and broken, and beyond it a shadow that might have been a ravine.

He had spent a lifetime learning to arrive. No one had taught him the first thing about surviving it. He started walking, counting his steps, because counting was something to do.

He crossed the rise at a stumble and from the crest saw it: a dark mound in the white, too regular to be rock. He went down. Snow had drifted against one flank; the matted coat held the animal’s shape like a cast. A woolly mammoth. Its trunk lay curled against the snow, one tusk sheared near the root. The body was whole—no cuts, no spear marks, no trampled ring where hunters had stood. Nothing had fed on it. It had lain down, or been caught, and the cold had kept it.

He stood a long time. The wind worked at his coat. He had aimed for the late Pleistocene—the caves, the fires, the people he had spent his life studying. This was older. Tens of thousands of years older. The jump had missed, or he had, and the error was not one he could walk back from. He had given everything to arrive, and here it was: a dead thing in the snow and no one to meet him.

He crouched. His hands were clumsy, but he worked a shard of rib free and tore a strip of hide from the flank, stiff as board. He wrapped the hide around his wrist and put the bone in his coat. Then he looked at the ravine beyond the rise and started walking.

The ravine narrowed as he followed it down, its walls rising until they pinched to a seam of shadow. There, where the stone had split and one slab leaned against another, he found a shallow overhang — no more than a shelf of rock, but it broke the wind, and that was the whole of his ambition now.

He wedged the rib shard upright at the mouth and packed snow against its base, then dragged more with his hands until his arms shook. The hide-wrapped wrist was useless for feeling; he worked by sight and stubbornness, sealing himself behind a low white wall with a bone in it, like an animal building its own grave. He laughed once, briefly, and the sound frightened him.

Inside, he drew out the device. It lay in his palm like a river stone, small and certain. He pressed the charger and waited, and the cold glass gave nothing — no glow, no hum, no answer. He tried again, and a third time, and then he did the arithmetic he had spent his life refusing to do. Decades. It would need decades to gather itself again, and the years here were not the years he had planned for. He put it away.

Dark came down like a lid. Then the sound: a weight moving over snow, deliberate, circling. It stopped. It sniffed. The mammoth's fat was on his coat, and the thing outside knew it, and it did not leave.
